World War II.outcome: Unconditional surrender of Germany (8 May 1945) and Japan (2 September 1945). The Allies (Soviet Union, United States, United Kingdom, China, France) won.
World War II.aftermath: Germany was occupied and partitioned into four zones, which became West Germany and East Germany. Japan was occupied by the United States until 1952. ~70 to 85 million people died, roughly 3 percent of the 1940 world population. The Holocaust killed ~6 million Jews and ~5 million others. The United Nations replaced the League of Nations, the Bretton Woods system reshaped global finance, and the Soviet Union and United States emerged as the two postwar superpowers. The trial of Nazi leaders at Nuremberg established the precedent that aggressive war and crimes against humanity are individually prosecutable.
World War II.keyTerms: Unconditional surrender. Signed at Reims (7 May), ratified at Karlshorst (8 May) for Germany. Signed aboard USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay (2 September) for Japan.
notable: Nuremberg and Tokyo war crimes trials
Partition of Germany and creation of the United Nations
Start of the nuclear age following Hiroshima and Nagasaki
Beginning of the Cold War

World War I.outcome: Armistice of Compiègne (11 November 1918, 11:00) ended fighting on the Western Front. The Allies (France, United Kingdom, United States, Italy, Russia until 1917) won.
World War I.aftermath: The Treaty of Versailles (1919) imposed reparations and territorial losses on Germany. The Austro-Hungarian, Ottoman, Russian, and German empires all collapsed and were replaced by republics or new states. ~20 million people died, roughly half of them civilians. The 1918 influenza pandemic, accelerated by wartime troop movement, killed another ~50 million. The League of Nations was founded but proved unable to prevent the next war.
World War I.keyTerms: Armistice (11 November 1918) followed by the Treaty of Versailles (28 June 1919), Treaty of Saint-Germain (Austria), Treaty of Trianon (Hungary), Treaty of Sèvres / Lausanne (Ottoman Empire).
notable: Collapse of four empires (German, Austro-Hungarian, Russian, Ottoman)
Creation of Poland, Czechoslovakia, Yugoslavia, and the Baltic states
Mandate system divides the former Ottoman lands
Russian Revolution removed Russia from the war in 1917

American Civil War.outcome: Confederate surrender at Appomattox Court House (9 April 1865) and Bennett Place (26 April 1865). The Union won.
American Civil War.aftermath: Slavery was abolished by the Thirteenth Amendment (December 1865). The Confederacy was dismantled and its states placed under Reconstruction, lasting until 1877. ~620,000 to 750,000 soldiers died, the deadliest war in United States history. Industrial economy of the North overwhelmed the agrarian South. Federal authority over states was decisively established, and the meaning of citizenship was rewritten by the Thirteenth, Fourteenth, and Fifteenth Amendments.
American Civil War.keyTerms: Surrender of the Army of Northern Virginia by Robert E. Lee to Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox, followed by piecemeal Confederate surrenders through May 1865.
notable: Assassination of Abraham Lincoln (14 April 1865) five days after Appomattox
Thirteenth, Fourteenth, and Fifteenth Amendments to the Constitution
Reconstruction era (1865 to 1877)
End of the institution of chattel slavery in the United States

Napoleonic Wars.outcome: Decisive Coalition victory at Waterloo (18 June 1815) ended Napoleon's Hundred Days. The Seventh Coalition (United Kingdom, Prussia, Austria, Russia, and others) won.
Napoleonic Wars.aftermath: Napoleon abdicated and was exiled to Saint Helena, where he died in 1821. The Congress of Vienna (1814 to 1815) redrew the map of Europe and restored the Bourbon monarchy in France. The Concert of Europe held off general European war for nearly a century. Roughly 3.5 to 6 million people died across two decades of conflict. Spanish American colonies, weakened by the long war, broke away over the following decade.
Napoleonic Wars.keyTerms: Treaty of Paris (1815) and the Congress of Vienna's Final Act (9 June 1815).
notable: Restoration of the Bourbons in France
Creation of the German Confederation
Loss of most Spanish colonies in the Americas over the next decade
Foundation of the post-1815 Concert of Europe

American Revolutionary War.outcome: British surrender at Yorktown (19 October 1781) effectively ended major combat. The Treaty of Paris (1783) recognized the independence of the United States.
American Revolutionary War.aftermath: Thirteen British colonies became the United States of America. Britain retained Canada and Caribbean possessions but lost its largest North American empire. The new United States adopted the Articles of Confederation, then the Constitution (1787). The example of a successful colonial republic influenced the French Revolution six years later.
American Revolutionary War.keyTerms: Treaty of Paris (3 September 1783), in which Britain recognized the independence of the United States and ceded territory east of the Mississippi.
notable: Birth of the United States as an independent republic
Adoption of the United States Constitution (1787)
Direct influence on the French Revolution and later wars of independence in the Americas

Vietnam War.outcome: Fall of Saigon (30 April 1975) to North Vietnamese forces. North Vietnam, the Viet Cong, and their allies won.
Vietnam War.aftermath: Vietnam was unified under the communist government in Hanoi as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam (1976). ~1 to 3 million Vietnamese died across two decades of war, plus ~58,000 American service members and significant losses in Laos and Cambodia. The Khmer Rouge took Cambodia in the same months and went on to kill ~1.5 to 2 million Cambodians. United States military and political confidence was deeply shaken, with effects on American foreign policy for a generation.
Vietnam War.keyTerms: Paris Peace Accords (27 January 1973) ended direct American involvement. The war between North and South Vietnam continued until Saigon fell on 30 April 1975 without a final treaty.
notable: Unification of Vietnam under the Hanoi government
Cambodian genocide under the Khmer Rouge (1975 to 1979)
Boat people exodus of refugees from Indochina
Lasting effect on American politics and military doctrine

Korean War.outcome: Korean Armistice Agreement (27 July 1953) suspended fighting along a line near the original 38th parallel. No peace treaty has ever been signed. The war ended in stalemate.
Korean War.aftermath: Korea remained divided between the Democratic People's Republic of Korea in the north and the Republic of Korea in the south. The Korean Demilitarized Zone runs roughly along the ceasefire line. ~3 million people died, most of them civilians. The war hardened the Cold War alliance system and brought the United States into a permanent military presence in East Asia.
Korean War.keyTerms: Armistice signed at Panmunjom on 27 July 1953 between the United Nations Command, North Korea, and the Chinese People's Volunteer Army. South Korea refused to sign.
notable: Permanent division of Korea at the Demilitarized Zone
First major proxy war of the Cold War
United States military presence in South Korea continues to the present
Technically still a state of war, not peace

War of 1812.outcome: Treaty of Ghent (24 December 1814) restored the pre-war borders. The war ended in a stalemate, though both sides claimed victory.
War of 1812.aftermath: United States borders with British North America were unchanged. The Battle of New Orleans (8 January 1815) was fought after the treaty was signed but before news reached the parties. Native American confederations in the Northwest and the South lost their most effective resistance to American expansion. Britain shifted its colonial focus toward what would become Canada.
War of 1812.keyTerms: Treaty of Ghent (24 December 1814), restoring status quo ante bellum.
notable: Burning of Washington by British forces (August 1814)
Andrew Jackson's victory at New Orleans (January 1815)
End of organized Native resistance east of the Mississippi
Beginning of nearly two centuries of unguarded United States to Canada border

Greco-Persian Wars.outcome: Decisive Greek victory. The Persian Empire ceased its westward expansion into the Aegean.
Greco-Persian Wars.aftermath: The Greek city-states emerged with a sense of common identity and growing confidence. Athens led the Delian League, which over the next half century became an Athenian empire and provoked the Peloponnesian War. The Persian Empire survived but never again seriously threatened Greece by land. The war shaped the Greek self-image of free city-states resisting eastern despotism, an idea revived throughout Western political thought.
Greco-Persian Wars.keyTerms: Peace of Callias (~449 BC, traditionally dated), in which Persia recognized Greek freedom in Asia Minor.
notable: Foundation of the Delian League under Athens
Beginning of the Athenian Golden Age
Long-running theme in Western political thought of free poleis against eastern empire

Eastern Front of World War II.outcome: Total Soviet victory. The Wehrmacht surrendered after the fall of Berlin (2 May 1945) and Germany's unconditional surrender at Reims and Karlshorst (7 to 8 May 1945).
Eastern Front of World War II.aftermath: Soviet forces occupied Eastern Europe and the eastern half of Germany. The Iron Curtain followed. ~26 to 27 million Soviet citizens died, the largest national death toll of any belligerent. Germany's Drang nach Osten ambitions ended permanently. The scale and brutality of fighting on the Eastern Front (over 80 percent of German army casualties) shaped Soviet society and politics for the rest of the century.
Eastern Front of World War II.keyTerms: Surrender at Karlshorst (8 May 1945), in Marshal Zhukov's headquarters in the eastern suburbs of Berlin.
notable: Battle of Stalingrad (1942 to 1943), turning point of the war
Battle of Kursk (1943), end of German offensive capability in the East
Operation Bagration (1944), destruction of Army Group Center
Soviet occupation of Eastern Europe and the Cold War division of the continent

Pacific War.outcome: Surrender of Japan (2 September 1945) aboard USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay. The Allies (United States, China, United Kingdom, Australia, and others) won.
Pacific War.aftermath: Japan was occupied by the United States under General Douglas MacArthur until 1952, with a new constitution and demilitarization imposed. Korea, Taiwan, Manchuria, and other Japanese-held territories were returned or transferred to other powers. The atomic bombings of Hiroshima (6 August) and Nagasaki (9 August) ended the war and opened the nuclear age. China resumed its civil war between Nationalists and Communists, won by the Communists in 1949.
Pacific War.keyTerms: Instrument of Surrender of Japan signed aboard USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay, 2 September 1945.
notable: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
United States occupation and democratization of Japan
Independence movements in Korea, Vietnam, Indonesia, and the Philippines
Chinese Civil War resumes, won by Mao Zedong in 1949

Russo-Ukrainian War.outcome: Ongoing as of mid-2026. No internationally recognized resolution. The full-scale Russian invasion began 24 February 2022.
Russo-Ukrainian War.aftermath: Hundreds of thousands of casualties on both sides. Several million Ukrainians displaced as refugees across Europe. NATO expanded to include Finland (2023) and Sweden (2024). Western sanctions reshaped European energy markets. The war is the largest in Europe since 1945 and remains undetermined.
Russo-Ukrainian War.keyTerms: No treaty. Ceasefires and exchanges have been local and partial.
notable: Largest interstate war in Europe since 1945
NATO expansion to include Finland and Sweden
European energy market restructured away from Russian gas
ICC arrest warrant issued for Vladimir Putin (March 2023)
